pipelines.move.stepRemoveDetail: After {minutes} minutes with every request on the new runtime
pipelines.move.downtimeKeep: Callers keep {address}. Both runtimes answer until the move ends, and a roll back puts every request back on {runtime}.
pipelines.move.costSame: The move changes nothing a month.
pipelines.move.costAdds: The move adds about {amount} a month.
pipelines.move.costSaves: The move saves about {amount} a month.
pipelines.move.costAssumes: Both runtimes are priced running one instance of {cpu} vCPU and {memory} GiB all month. Requests, data, discounts and free tiers change the real bill.
pipelines.move.title: Move {application} to {runtime}
pipelines.frontDoor.title: Front door
pipelines.frontDoor.intro: A stable address per environment, so applications move between runtimes with no downtime
pipelines.frontDoor.none: No front door serves {application} yet. An admin turns one on in Platform › Environments.
pipelines.frontDoor.hostHeader: Call it with the Host header {host}
pipelines.frontDoor.off: Off. A switch of runtime here waits for the next deploy, and the address changes.
pipelines.frontDoor.addresses: {count} addresses, one in each project. Each application's page shows its own
pipelines.frontDoor.addressLater: The address is reserved when the first application is released here
pipelines.frontDoor.noDomain: No domain: HTTP on the address
pipelines.frontDoor.problemsLabel: What the front door in {env} needs
pipelines.frontDoor.dialogDescription: One load balancer for the environment, with a host for each application released there.
pipelines.frontDoor.domainHint: Each application answers on its own name under {domain}, over HTTPS once DNS points at the address and Google issues its certificate.
pipelines.frontDoor.domainNone: Without one, applications answer over HTTP on the address, each called with its key as the Host header.
pipelines.frontDoor.domainInvalid: Name a domain such as prod.example.com
pipelines.frontDoor.offMeans: Turning it off takes the load balancer down. Applications keep running where they are, at their own addresses.
pipelines.runtimes.frontDoorMove: A switch takes effect on the next deploy. Where a front door serves it, a switch plans a move with no downtime instead.
pipelines.runtimes.movePlanned: Move to {runtime} planned. Review the plan
pipelines.capacity.autopilotAdded: Pods start on GKE Autopilot when jobs wait in this pool, once its cluster is ready. No token is needed.
pipelines.capacity.kindAutopilotHint: Pipelines starts one pod per job on a cluster in your CI project, and none while nothing waits.
pipelines.capacity.podBuilderHint: Image builds run in this image beside the runner. Leave it empty for Kaniko.
pipelines.capacity.podClusterCreateHint: The Autopilot cluster the pool's pods run on, in this project.
pipelines.capacity.podClusterHint: An Autopilot cluster that exists in this project.
pipelines.capacity.podClusterInvalid: Use lowercase letters, digits and dashes, starting with a letter
pipelines.capacity.podCpuInvalid: Use 0.5 to 28 vCPU, in quarter steps
pipelines.capacity.podCreate: Create the cluster if it is missing
pipelines.capacity.podCreateHint: Pipelines creates an Autopilot cluster with this name in the project. It takes several minutes.
pipelines.capacity.podImageHint: The runner's gke image, pushed to your Artifact Registry.
pipelines.capacity.podMemoryInvalid: Use 1 to 6.5 GiB for each vCPU, and at most 80
pipelines.capacity.podServiceAccountHint: Pods act as this account through Workload Identity, to push images and deploy.
pipelines.capacity.podSizeHint: Each step image in a job gets this much. Autopilot bills by what pods ask for.
pipelines.capacity.podSpotHint: Costs less. Google may take a pod back, and its job then fails.
pipelines.capacity.podWarmHint: Room for this many stays warm on the nodes. 0 scales to zero.
pipelines.capacity.podsNow: {running, number} running · {starting, number} starting · {warm, number} warm
